newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo says time not right to release copper probe.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo says time not right to release copper probe.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp said on Friday the time was not right to release the results of an internal probe into its massive copper trading losses.

The company said at its annual shareholders' meeting in Osaka on Friday that it did not want to make public the probe right now because of the ongoing trial against its former star trader who is at the centre of the scandal and because of investigations by overseas authorities.

"The company and shareholders' interests could be damaged if we make our finding public right now. We'll release it at the right time," Takashi Nomura, the firm's senior managing director, told shareholders.

In June 1996, Sumitomo sent shock waves through the financial world by revealing massive losses from unauthorised copper trading by former star trader Yasuo Hamanaka, which eventually snowballed to $2.6 billion.
Since then, the giant trade house said it has carried out an in-house inquiry into the losses and is fully cooperating with U.S. and British authorities.
